MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center

Patient: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
Specimen: Peripheral blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Rule out Fragile X syndrome

TEST PERFORMED
PCR assay for FRAXA and FRAXE expansion mutations

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from peripheral blood. PCR amplification was performed using fluorescently labeled primers flanking the CGG repeat region in the FMR1 gene (FRAXA locus) and the GCC repeat region in the FMR2 gene (FRAXE locus). Fragment analysis was performed by capillary electrophoresis to determine the number of repeats. This assay can detect normal, intermediate, and premutation size alleles. Full mutations may not be reliably detected by this method.

RESULTS

FRAXA locus (FMR1 gene):
Allele 1: 29 CGG repeats
Allele 2: 31 CGG repeats
Result: Normal sized alleles detected

FRAXE locus (FMR2 gene):
Allele 1: 16 GCC repeats
Allele 2: 18 GCC repeats
Result: Normal sized alleles detected

INTERPRETATION
Normal sized alleles were detected at both the FRAXA and FRAXE loci. These results indicate that the patient is unlikely to be affected with Fragile X syndrome based on the presence of normal sized alleles.

Reference ranges:
FRAXA: Normal <45 CGG repeats; Intermediate 45-54; Premutation 55-200; Full mutation >200
FRAXE: Normal <31 GCC repeats; Intermediate 31-60; Full mutation >200

LIMITATIONS
This PCR-based assay may not detect large full mutations or mosaicism. If clinical suspicion remains high, Southern blot analysis may be considered.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
